# Palette (generated by tools/palette_check.py from style.py; do not edit by hand)

One palette for every figure; `style.py` is the only place colours are defined, and every plotting module imports it. Preview with simulated colour-vision deficiency: [palette_preview.png](palette_preview.png).

## Rules

* **Demand bands** are coloured by the pathway that targets them: Extra space in the P1 colour; Vacancy and 2026 overbuild in the P2 family; Historical replacement and Recent replacement surge in the P3 family. The untargeted bands (Population growth, Smaller households) are neutral greys with a light dot hatch, so they read as untargeted without colour. Maintenance (B2, B4) within 2026-2050 is a light tint of the P4 colour (material carbon).
* **P4** (Low-carbon materials) marks intensity and material effects; Materials and construction (A1-A5) take the P4 colour in the component figure.
* **Reference** dark grey (#4D4D4D); **TL** near-black (#141414); TL gradual adoption light grey (#A6A6A6); Low and High replacement mid greys with dashed and dotted lines.
* **Boundaries**: acquired rights (AR) blue solid (#1F5FA8), ability to pay (AtP) orange dashed (#C2571A); the two principles are never shaded as a range and never averaged.
* **Settings**: Moderate solid line or open marker; Ambitious dashed line or filled marker (bars: Moderate bars, Ambitious whiskers).
* **Typeface**: Liberation Sans only (metric-compatible with Arial), bundled in `fonts/` under the SIL Open Font License 1.1, registered by style.py, so every machine renders the same glyphs.
* **Sizes** (Nature Cities): width 89 mm (single column) or 183 mm (double column), page depth at most 247 mm; text 7 pt, legends and ticks 6 pt, never below 5 pt; data lines 1 pt, emphasised lines 1.5 pt, grid and edges 0.5 pt.
* **Files**: PNG at 300 dpi for every figure; vector PDF (TrueType fonts embedded) for the headline figures; no software or date metadata, so re-runs are byte-identical.
* **Materials** (H4b and the diagnostics): the six stripes of the Pride flag in one order in every figure (author decision, baseline-pb-v2), soil carbon loss faded and hatched on top; kept because the material figures label every layer directly (see the check below).

## Colour-vision-deficiency check

Minimum pairwise distance within each group (CAM02-UCS, Luo, Cui & Li 2006) after simulating the deficiency at full severity (Machado, Oliveira & Fernandes 2009; colorspacious 1.1.2). Threshold for "clearly distinguishable" adjacent fills: 10 (stated convention).

|---|---|---|---|---|---|

## Sequential ramp

Continuous fields (the solution space, H10) use one blue ramp, light to dark; its CAM02-UCS lightness J' must fall strictly so the order survives greyscale: `#EAF2FB` 96, `#C6DBF2` 88, `#9EC5F4` 80, `#6DA7EC` 69, `#3987E5` 57, `#256ABF` 46, `#184F95` 35, `#0D366B` 24 (monotone).

## Sources

* Luo MR, Cui G, Li C (2006) Uniform colour spaces based on CIECAM02 colour appearance model. Color Research & Application 31, 320-330.
* Machado GM, Oliveira MM, Fernandes LAF (2009) A physiologically-based model for simulation of color vision deficiency. IEEE Transactions on Visualization and Computer Graphics 15, 1291-1298.
* Okabe M, Ito K (2008) Color Universal Design (CUD): how to make figures and presentations that are friendly to colorblind people. https://jfly.uni-koeln.de/color/ (the categorical palette).
* Smith NJ, van der Walt S, colorspacious 1.1.2 (Python package), https://github.com/njsmith/colorspacious.
